rows.speaker: في ظلال القرآن
rows.claim: The human spirit can rise beyond the angels when it follows its innate nature and faith, but can fall below every creature when it abandons them; believers preserve and perfect that nature.
rows.anchor: جاء في ظلال القرآن: "والتركيز في هذا المقام على خصائصه الروحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse accommodates the reported readings and also implies that unbelievers live in distress, as linked to the constricted life of 20:124 and the falling image in 22:31.
rows.anchor: وظاهر أن معنى الآية يتسع لكل ما ذكروه، وهي تفيد أيضاً أن حياة غير المؤمن نكد وغمّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Tin exception concerns deliverance from the depths of Hell, so faith and good works suffice; al-Asr concerns loss, where omitting mutual exhortation forfeits additional reward.
rows.anchor: وذلك لاختلاف الموطنين، فإن سورة العصر في بيان الخسران الذي يصيب الإنسان، وسورة التين فيما يُنجي من دركات النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who believes and acts righteously but does not exhort others loses reward he could have earned, without necessarily being among those brought to the lowest state.
rows.anchor: فإن كلّ من ترك شيئاً من ذلك خسر شيئاً من الأجر الذي كان يربحه فيما لو فعله

rows.speaker: التبيان
rows.claim: Al-Tibyan explains that al-Asr narrows its exception to include mutual exhortation, while al-Tin broadens its exception; exhortation adds to personal faith and good works, and its omission means loss without requiring descent to the lowest state.
rows.anchor: جاء في (التبيان) : "وتأمل حكمة القرآن لما قال

rows.speaker: التبيان
rows.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong may be individually obligatory, communal, or recommended; mutual counsel covers obligatory and recommended truth and patience, earning reward beyond personal duty, so partial loss differs from total loss.
rows.anchor: فمطلق الخسار شيء والخسار المطلق شيء (التبيان 91)

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported meaning of “unfailing” reward is that it is neither diminished nor interrupted.
rows.anchor: قيل: ومعنى غير ممنون غير منقوص ولا منقطع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported meaning is that the reward is not marred by reminding the recipients of the favor.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه غير مكدر بالمنّ عليهم (البحر المحيط 8/490، روح المعاني 30/176)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He accepts both senses: the reward neither ends nor is spoiled by reminders of favor.
rows.anchor: والحق أن كل ذلك مراد وهو من صفات الثواب، لأنه يجب أن يكون غير منقطع ولا منغصاً بالمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ghayr mamnun gathers both senses, whereas “not cut off” or similar wording would convey only one.
rows.anchor: فقال: (غير ممنون) ليجمع هذه المعاني كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tin adds fa before the reward because its context does not explicitly identify the people returned low, while al-Inshiqaq describes disbelievers at length and its believers briefly, making omission of fa suit that brevity.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر كيف زاد الفاء في قوله (فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says only that the human is returned to the lowest state and does not explicitly restrict the referent to disbelievers or another group.
rows.anchor: يعني الإنسان، وهو غير صريح في أن المقصود به الكافرون أو غيرهم كما أسلفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Inshiqaq begins with human toil and successive hardships, whereas Tin begins by honoring humanity; this makes the added fa fit the affirmation that the reward continues without being marred.
rows.anchor: في حين بدأ في سورة التين بتكريم الإنسان فقال (لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ (4) التين) فناسب ذلك تأكيد استمرار أجره وعدم تنغيصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this clear proof, what could make a person deny requital? Human creation from a drop, sound formation, and development to maturity demonstrate the Creator's power to resurrect; the first creation would not have occurred if return were beyond Him.
rows.anchor: أي شيء يجعلك أيها الإنسان مكذّباً بالجزاء بعد هذا الدليل الواضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument for requital combines transmitted evidence from the major divine messages of Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad with rational evidence from human creation and its stages of development.
rows.anchor: فالدليل النقلي هو ما أخبرت به الرسالات السماوية، وقد ذكر من هذه الرسالات كبراها وهي رسالات موسى وعيسى ومحمد
